title: s(157) below 13 and a new s(132): two pinwheel packings: registration request
body:
**Credit name.** Joost de Winter

**Claim.** Two upper bounds, each below the value in the register (repository state of 11 November 2026, commit c844872).

| n | New side | Register | Gain |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | ---: |
| 157 | 12.99330261134322364133727935496577166311874424252458... | 13 (grid) | 6.70e-3 |
| 132 | 11.97604838360340752372871695271367782454646197183552... | 11.9856801988458088115 | 9.63e-3 |

As far as the register shows, the first is the first reported packing of 157 unit squares in a square of side below 13.

**Type of result.** Both are new arrangements at their counts. Each is a pinwheel: a central block of tilted squares with four arms, surrounded by four blocks of axis-aligned squares.

**Certificate.** https://github.com/JoostdeWinter/square-packing/tree/6617869a3491b5872c6ecdff55db05cbee57d516 (folders `n157` and `n132`)
- `nNNN_exact.json`: exact rational centres and unit edge directions, and the side.
- `nNNN_witness.yaml`: the same packing in the witness format (center-basis, rational).
- `verify_exact.py`: exact checker (Python 3.10 or later, standard library only).

**Checking.** `verify_exact.py` checks in rational arithmetic that every edge direction is a unit vector, that every square lies in the container, and that all pairs have disjoint interiors. Two further checks agree: a floating-point separating-axis test on all pairs, and a union-area test with Shapely (157.0000000000 and 132.0000000000).

**What the checkers share.** The exact checker is the one used for #946, without the polynomial test. It has not been run against this project's checkers. The two further checks are separate code and are outside the repository.

**Not done.** Local optimality has no formal proof. The evidence is numerical. All squares were optimized together with an interior-point solver (IPOPT). The contact equations were then solved to 250 digits: 2024 equations at n = 157 are satisfied to 1e-247 and 1407 equations at n = 132 to 1e-269. Balanced non-negative contact forces exist (floating point). In 297 and 324 perturbation trials with re-optimization, no smaller side came up. The certificates are 1.4e-59 and 1.3e-59 above the high-precision solutions. A search for a minimal polynomial of the side up to degree 16 found none at either count. I have not seen the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard values for these counts, so unpublished packings with a smaller side may exist.

**Lineage and credit.** The seed is the public packing of 109 unit squares in `Samanyu-dev/squares_in_squares` at commit 53551d77513a9f5c180a731f291baf7eda7c3009 (file `best_fit_101_500.csv`, side 10.949289581, below the register's 10.949747468 for n = 109). The README of that repository reports it as a result of its own stretch and quench chains. I make no claim at n = 109. One step cuts the packing along one horizontal and one vertical line, moves the parts about one unit apart, fills each gap with one layer of squares that continues the local lattice, and re-optimizes all squares. One step gives the packing of 132 squares, and a second step gives the packing of 157 squares. Credit for the pinwheel arrangement at n = 109 belongs to Samanyu-dev. My contribution is the two growth steps and the optimization.

**AI assistance.** The derivation, optimization, high-precision solution, rational certificates, checks and figures were produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) under my direction.
